This method computes the in-scattered single scattering radiance $J_{ss}$ by approximating the phase function and incident radiance with low-order expansions, allowing the scattering contribution to be decomposed into direction-independent terms that are pre-computed per voxel [S1].

The claim states that the method computes in-scattered single scattering radiance $J_{ss}$ by approximating the phase function and incident radiance with low-order expansions, allowing the scattering contribution to be decomposed into direction-independent terms that are pre-computed per voxel. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.1.3 and 3.1.4: it approximates the phase function using a truncated Legendre polynomial expansion (first moment) and the incident radiance using a first-order Taylor expansion. It then shows that substituting these into the rendering equation allows $J_{ss}$ to be decomposed into direction-independent terms ($Q_{ri}^0$ and $Q_{ri}^1$) which are pre-computed for each voxel during a preprocessing step (Algorithm 1) to avoid repeated ray tracing.
